title: Dental Implants With Bone Loss: Options & Cost Guide
seoTitle: Dental Implants With Bone Loss: Your Options
seoDescription: Bone loss rarely rules out implants. Learn how CBCT planning, grafting, short implants and overdentures can help. Book a Valencia evaluation.
excerpt: Bone loss used to rule out implants. Here is how CBCT evaluation, grafting, sinus lifts, short implants and overdentures make them possible for many patients.
keyTakeaways: A CBCT scan plus clinical exam measures bone height and width and decides whether grafting, a sinus lift or short implants are needed.
Options include localized grafting, sinus lift, short or narrow implants, zygomatic implants and implant-retained overdentures.
Grafting typically adds two to six months before implant placement, though some cases allow graft and implant at the same time.
The article reports implant survival after grafting in the high 80s to mid 90s percent at five to ten years.
Smoking, uncontrolled diabetes and certain medications raise the risk of graft failure and peri-implant problems.
